events.quote: use at with a clock time ..., on with a day or date ..., and in with a month or year
Right: The lesson is at 9 o'clock. Wrong: The lesson is in 9 o'clock.
use some in positive sentences ... and any in negative sentences and questions
Right: I don't have any money. Wrong: I don't have some money.
Right: The lesson is at 9 o'clock. Wrong: The lesson is in 9 o'clock.
after he, she or it, the verb takes -s
Add -es after sh, ch, s, x and o ... Do not add -s after I, you, we or they.
Right: She watches TV. Wrong: She watchs TV.
